title: Design System: ECO SERVICE · The journey of one application

display.purpose: ECO SERVICE on the opening and closing steps.

headline.purpose: The centered statement over the open map.

headline-sm.purpose: The top-anchored heading above the eight-station overview and the finale.

lead.purpose: The hero's one line under the wordmark.

body.purpose: Card sentences; 1.4rem centered and 1.3rem top-anchored over the open map.

title-sm.purpose: Station names in diagrams; sheet, panel and row titles at 0.95-1.05rem.

label.purpose: Sub-lines under station names and sheet titles; map tags.

note.purpose: The source or illustration note at a card's foot.

paper-title.purpose: The capitalized title of an official paper.

data.purpose: Martian Mono for values the system holds: application number, coordinates, counter, numerals, score.

shadows.name: card-hang
shadows.purpose: The narrative card, paired with backdrop-filter: blur(14px) saturate(1.15).

shadows.name: paper-hang
shadows.purpose: Official papers; the tight second layer gives the sheet a physical edge.

shadows.name: now-halo
shadows.purpose: The current rail station; larger stations widen the ring to 6-7px.

shadows.name: line-glow
shadows.purpose: The rail fill; SVG routes use drop-shadow(0 0 6px rgba(98, 215, 234, 0.55)), leaf and coral routes their own hue at 0.5.

shadows.name: pulse-core
shadows.purpose: The core of the application's pulse on the map (leaf variant at 0.7).

shadows.name: map-text-halo
shadows.purpose: text-shadow for text sitting straight on the map; the counter and mark use 0.6rem and 1.4rem.

shadows.name: statement-shadow
shadows.purpose: text-shadow for centered and top-anchored statements over the open map.

motion.name: ease-expo
motion.purpose: House curve for CSS state changes: chrome fades 0.8s, rail 0.9s, rail fill 1.2s, station states 0.6s, marker reveals 0.7-0.9s.

motion.name: card-enter
motion.value: 0.8s expo.out from y 18px; children 1.05s expo.out from y 20px and blur(8px), stagger 0.08s

motion.name: visual-exit
motion.purpose: A visual leaving when the next step changes its type.

motion.name: pop
motion.value: 0.7s expo.out from y 14px, stagger 0.08s; nodes back.out(1.7), chips back.out(2)

motion.name: line-draw
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset 0.8-1.3s power2.inOut; the token rides the same path, power1.inOut
motion.purpose: Routes drawing on in transit diagrams.

motion.name: camera-follow
motion.purpose: Cameras that follow the application along its route.

motion.name: map-paint
motion.purpose: Layer opacity and saturation changes between steps.

motion.name: route-grow
motion.value: 2.6s power2.inOut after 0.35s (3.2s when the head travels the whole route)
motion.purpose: The route extending stage by stage.

motion.name: ambient-sway
motion.value: bearing within drift x 8 degrees, 46s sine
motion.purpose: Keeps a landed camera alive; off under reduced motion and ?still.

motion.name: pulse-ping
motion.value: 2.6s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.6, 0.3, 1) infinite, scale 1 to 6, two rings 1.3s apart
motion.purpose: The application's pulse on the map.

motion.name: press
motion.value: scale 0.93 over 0.14s power2.in, back to 1 over 0.5s back.out(3)

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Cameras jump, timelines land on their end state, pulse rings stop.

components.name: Narrative Card

components.html:

A school building is planned in the Fergana Valley. Its application enters the system as No. 371668581.

Sample application and site coordinates from the ECO SERVICE process deck.

narrative.overview:
The system is a night earth and one lit line. A single application travels over the real satellite map of Uzbekistan, from a 10 m plot in the Fergana Valley to Tashkent and back, and every screen is a station on that line. The ground is a slate-black night with the country's border lit in the shield's cyan and the rest of the world masked; the process is drawn in transit-map grammar (tracks, lit routes, ring stations, a fork, a loop, a transfer); system screens arrive as dark sheets and official documents as pale paper.

Density is low and cinematic: one heading, one or two sentences, at most one evidence block per step, at sizes that read across a hall. Color is a status code, not decoration: Lit Cyan is the system and where the application is now, leaf is done, amber is waiting, coral is returned. Motion is camera flight and line drawing; between steps the earth sways a few degrees so a held step never looks frozen.

The direction refuses the category default, process boxes and arrows on a white slide. Where the build departs from the direction contract, the build is recorded here: the opening crest is 6.4rem (the contract asked for about 7rem) and the wordmark 5.6rem (about 5.4rem). The contract's "official sheets" became two materials in the build: pale paper for documents, dark sheets for system screens.
keyCharacteristics: Night satellite earth as the only ground: imagery desaturated and capped, Uzbekistan's border lit, everything outside it masked.
Transit-diagram grammar for every process: 3px tracks, 4px lit routes, ring stations, a fork, a loop, a transfer.
A four-state color code from the shield: cyan current, leaf done, amber waiting, coral returned.
Two materials for evidence: dark translucent system sheets and flat pale paper for official documents.
Geologica for every word; Martian Mono only for values the system holds.
Type and spacing locked to screen height (1rem = min(1.9vh, 1.07vw)), composed at 1920×1080.
Camera flights and drawn lines carry the motion; a slow, bounded sway keeps the earth alive between steps.

rules.name: The Status-Only Hue Rule
rules.body: Leaf, amber and coral are states, never accents: leaf is done or approved, amber is waiting, coral is returned. If nothing has happened to it, it does not wear them.

rules.name: The Two Cyans Rule
rules.body: Lit Cyan draws whatever must be read or followed on the night ground: lines, rings, icons, IDs and their glows. Shield Cyan is the brand's own cyan, used broad and soft: blooms, area fills, washes, halos. Shield Cyan never sets a word.

rules.name: The Paper-Is-Official Rule
rules.body: Official Paper is reserved for documents the state records or issues: the application record, the expertise conclusion, the signed conclusion. System screens are always dark sheets.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono sets only values the system holds: the application number, coordinates, step and station numerals, field numbers, the score and its scale, the 15–25 span on the finale rail. The words around a value stay Geologica, even inside one line ("Application No." in Geologica, the number in Mono). Numbers inside headlines and sentences stay Geologica.

rules.name: The Tighten-As-It-Grows Rule
rules.body: Headings tighten and thicken as they grow: -0.028em at 2.45rem, -0.035em at 3.4rem, -0.038em at 4.4rem, -0.04em at 5.6rem, weight rising from 620 to 720. Body text is never tracked.

rules.name: The Form-Title Rule
rules.body: Spaced capitals (0.08em, 700) belong to official paper titles alone. Nothing on a dark surface is set in spaced capitals.

rules.name: The Height-Locked Rem Rule
rules.body: Size everything that composes the frame in rem (1rem = min(1.9vh, 1.07vw)) and compose at 1920×1080; HTML type is never sized in px.

rules.name: The Subject-In-The-Clear Rule
rules.body: The camera frames its subject in the ground the card leaves free, never behind the card; while the application rides, it holds the band under the top bar.

rules.name: The Hanging Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface that floats over the map hangs: a large downward offset, a large blur and a negative spread at 0.8–0.95 black, so it darkens the ground beneath it without a visible halo edge.

rules.name: The Light-Is-State Rule
rules.body: Among routes, stations and choices, glow marks the live thing: the route, the current station, the application's pulse, the chosen answer. Finished stations go flat in leaf; on the docked rail and in diagrams, stations not yet reached are idle hairline rings.

rules.name: The Veil-Under-The-Light Rule
rules.body: Dim the ground only through the in-map veil, beneath the border, route and markers. The shade scrim above the map only grades the frame's edges for the card, rail and chrome; nothing flat is laid over the whole map to darken it.

rules.name: The Solid Route Rule
rules.body: The application's route is a solid, round-capped 4px line, and its lit head (pulse and number tag) rides the tip until the application arrives, when the destination's pulse takes over. Dashes belong to the inspection ring alone, which marks an area, not a path.

dos: Do draw every process as a transit line: a 3px Track, a 4px Lit Cyan route, ring stations in their state colors, a fork for simultaneous routing, a coral loop for revision, a framed transfer for coordination.
Do keep the one application in view: its pulse and number tag mark where it is (the site, then the route's tip), held in the band under the top bar while a visual is up.
Do draw official documents as flat Official Paper (3px corners, crest, numbered hairline-ruled fields or sections, signature lines on what gets signed) and every system screen as a dark sheet.
Do set every value the system holds in Martian Mono and every word in Geologica, splitting within a line where they meet.
Do dim through the in-map veil (0.45–0.75, saturation down to -0.6) so the border, route and markers stay lit above it.
Do halo any text that sits straight on the map with Night Ground (0 0 0.5rem and 0 0 1.2rem).
Do label illustrative screens and sample data with a source note at the card's foot (0.74rem, Haze Ink).
Do step back what is no longer the point by fading it to 0.28–0.38 opacity rather than removing it.
Do keep every word as live text so the deck can be translated; no text is baked into images.
donts: Don't draw the process as boxes and arrows on a white slide.
Don't put leaf, amber or coral on anything that is not a state.
Don't set words in Martian Mono, or the numbers inside headlines and sentences.
Don't draw the application's route dashed or thinner than 4px; dashes belong to the inspection ring alone.
Don't darken the whole map with a flat layer above it; it would bury the lit route and markers. Above the map, only the shade scrim grades the frame's edges.
Don't make a system screen light or an official document dark.
Don't set spaced capitals anywhere but an official paper's title, or put a label above a card's heading.
Don't give elements hover states; state comes from the step, and the pointer hides.
Don't size HTML type in px; the height-locked rem keeps the composition identical on every screen.
